audit.whatIsWrong: All seven phases[N].side read "Fizz" while content win[0..6] and the packet levelChart both read Orianna, Skill x5, Orianna. Every row rendered two answers, and rows 1-5 additionally had Orianna-favourable sentences sitting under a Fizz verdict.
audit.why: Level 1 is Orianna's: Urchin Strike is a 550-range dash and she pokes from 815 with a stacking passive. Levels 2-5 are a bait war — Seastone Trident's empowered attack against Q-W trades, and from 3 the Playful / Trickster hop goes untargetable on 16s falling to 8s. Level 6 gives him a 1300-range Chum the Waters but gives her Shockwave. At 2+ items he has to land inside the team he is diving, which is where Command: Shockwave wins.
audit.corrected: phases[0].side = Orianna, phases[1..5].side = Skill at 5/10, phases[6].side = Orianna, with all five middle whys rewritten so the sentence matches the even verdict instead of describing Orianna running the lane.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.spikes named no Fizz spike and carried an unsourced magnitude ("Luden's makes Q-W a third of a health bar").
audit.why: His spike curve is the Playful / Trickster cooldown, 16s at rank 1 down to 8s at rank 5, and Chum the Waters at 120/100/80 with 1300 range.
audit.corrected: Spike line rebuilt on the hop cooldown and the level 6 shark.

audit.why: The page's core read is right: Playful / Trickster makes Fizz untargetable, so it eats a committed Command: Attack or Command: Shockwave outright. What was missing is the number that makes the advice actionable — 16s at rank 1 against a 7s Q at rank 1, so one thrown ball genuinely can buy the window.
audit.corrected: Cooldowns attached to the bait instruction everywhere it appears.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page mentions Nimble Fighter.
audit.why: Fizz takes a flat amount of reduced damage from every source. Against an Orianna gameplan built on repeated chip — ball Q, passive autos, Dissonance ticks — a flat reduction applied per instance costs proportionally more than it does against burst. It is the reason poke does not close him out the way it closes out other mids.
audit.corrected: Stated in breakdown.early so the reader knows why the poke plan under-delivers here.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page never tells the reader what his combo looks like before it lands.
audit.why: Seastone Trident empowers his next attack, so the burst opens with an auto wind-up rather than a visible cast — the wind-up is the cue to step back. Flagged as autoreset-burst-tell in _missing for this matchup.
Playful / Trickster 16/14/12/10/8, Seastone Trident 7/6/5/4/3, Urchin Strike 8/7.5/7/6.5/6, Chum the Waters 120/100/80; Command: Protect 9s, Command: Shockwave 110/95/80.

notes: Chart was fully desynced: every phases[N].side said Fizz while content and the packet said Orianna / Skill x5 / Orianna. I aligned full to the two agreeing sources and rewrote all five middle whys, because leaving Orianna-running-the-lane sentences under an even verdict would have swapped one contradiction for another. Ratings on the five Skill rows set to 5/10 to match the Skill convention used elsewhere in this champion's data. report[8].t named Zed in a Fizz matchup — a template leak, now pointed at Fizz's own level 6. Added Nimble Fighter, which appeared nowhere: the flat per-instance damage reduction is specifically why an Orianna chip gameplan under-delivers into him. UNVERIFIED, left out of the page deliberately: the derived flags on fizz.json mark both Playful / Trickster and Chum the Waters as "grounding", but Riot's own text for neither ability mentions grounding. Per the brief I trusted the description and wrote nothing about it — if grounding is real on the shark it would matter to a lot of mid matchups and is worth confirming once against the wiki.
